# MLT, SMLT, vIST and LACP

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 18 commands_

Link aggregation (static MLT and LACP) and dual-homing with SMLT over a virtual IST (vIST) through the fabric.

## Details

### `show smlt mlt`

An SMLT whose peer side shows down only works single-homed. Check the vIST and the MLT on the peer.


### `show virtual-ist`

The vIST runs through the fabric, so it is up as long as there is SPBM connectivity between the peers. If it is down, check IS-IS between the peers, the vIST VLAN I-SID (must be the same on both peers and unique in the fabric), the IP subnet and the ARP to the peer IP.


### `show virtual-ist stat`

Clear them with `clear virtual-ist stats` and check whether hellos still arrive.


### `show lacp interface [gigabitethernet <ports> | mlt]`

`show lacp actor-oper interface` and `show lacp partner-oper interface` show both sides in detail. A port that does not aggregate usually has a key mismatch or a partner without LACP.


### `show interfaces gigabitEthernet statistics lacp [<ports>]`

If the received count stays at 0, the partner sends no LACP.


### `mlt <id> enable name "<name>" / mlt <id> member <ports>`

```
mlt 10 enable name "SRV-ESX01"
mlt 10 member 1/10,2/10
mlt 10 encapsulation dot1q
vlan mlt 100 10
```

MLT names cannot be only digits. For SMLT, configure the same MLT ID on both vIST peers.


### `lacp enable key <key> (interface mlt)`

```
mlt 20 enable name "SW-ACCESS-12"
interface mlt 20
  lacp enable key 20
  exit
interface gigabitEthernet 1/20,2/20
  lacp key 20
  lacp aggregation enable
  lacp timeout-time short
  lacp enable
```

The recipe: port key, port aggregation enable, port lacp enable, then an MLT with the same key. Enable LACP globally too (`lacp enable` in Global Config). Once LACP is enabled you cannot add or remove ports by hand. VLANs added to an LACP MLT only reach the active ports, so add the VLAN to the inactive members as well.


### `lacp key <key> / lacp aggregation enable / lacp enable (interface)`

Further options are `lacp mode active|passive` and `lacp timeout-time short|long`. The timeout must match the partner.


### `lacp smlt-sys-id <mac>`

Without a common system ID, the downstream device sees two different partners and only bundles the links to one peer.


### `spbm 1 smlt-peer-system-id <peer-system-id>`

```
no router isis enable
router isis
  spbm 1 smlt-peer-system-id 0200.0001.0102
  spbm 1 smlt-virtual-bmac 02:00:00:01:01:ff
  exit
router isis enable
```

IS-IS must be disabled for this. If you use manual system-ids, also set the virtual B-MAC (`spbm 1 smlt-virtual-bmac`), the same on both peers. With default system-ids it is derived (lower system-id + 0x01). The peer with the lower system-id becomes the primary split-BEB.

> ▲ **Caution:** Disabling IS-IS takes the switch out of the fabric for the duration of the change.


### `virtual-ist peer-ip <peer-ip> vlan <vist-vlan>`

```
vlan create 4000 name "VIST" type port-mstprstp 0
vlan i-sid 4000 15999000
interface vlan 4000
  ip address 10.255.255.1 255.255.255.252
  exit
virtual-ist peer-ip 10.255.255.2 vlan 4000
```

The vIST VLAN needs an I-SID that is used nowhere else in the fabric, and a subnet shared only by the two peers. The vIST needs both the smlt-peer-system-id and the peer-ip.


### `smlt (interface mlt)`

```
interface mlt 10
  smlt
  exit
```

Every VLAN on an SMLT must have an I-SID, and the same VLAN/I-SID must exist on the peer, even if nothing is connected there.
